**390 instances across 333 servers.** Keyed on `ci.name` (`INSTANCE@server`), **not** `host.name` — `host.name` here is one of four collectors, with 86% of traffic on a single one.

Source is `metricbeat-*`, the legacy pre-data-stream indices. These documents are **not in `metrics-*`**, which is why an earlier review of this cluster concluded MSSQL was not collected at all.

**Three things on this dashboard are deliberately not what the raw fields say:**

- **The `*_per_sec` fields are not rates.** `batch_requests_per_sec` sampled at **9,694,126** and `logins_per_sec` at **281,543**, with logouts almost identical — those are cumulative counters from `sys.dm_os_performance_counters`, not per-second values. The Throughput panel derives true rates as *(max − min) ÷ elapsed seconds* per instance. A counter reset from an instance restart inside the window will distort that row.
- **`buffer.cache_hit.pct` is omitted.** It sampled at **2.2**, and a real SQL Server buffer cache hit ratio is 95–99%. The field is the raw counter without its `_base` divisor and cannot be corrected here.
- **`transaction_log.space_usage.used.pct` is already 0–100**, unlike the percentage fields elsewhere in this cluster. Verified against the byte fields: 52.9 MB of 39,240 MB reads 0.135.
